origin.details: True when which is among the object's attribute names. on_failure stores its handler as the attribute fail, so has_attr(has_attr, "fail") is true.
origin.example:
has_attr(has_attr, "fail")
x <- 10
x %has_attr% "a"

y <- list(a = 1, b = 2)
see_if(y %has_name% "c")

translation.details: True when which is among the object's attribute names. on_failure stores its handler as the attribute fail, so has_attr(has_attr, "fail") is true.
translation.example:
from assertthat import has_attr, see_if

print(has_attr(has_attr, "fail"))
x = 10
print(see_if('x %has_attr% "a"'))

y = {"a": 1, "b": 2}
print(see_if('y %has_name% "c"'))
